title: Implement an In-Memory LRU Cache for the LexiLearn Feature Store
description: The LexiLearn MVC Orchestrator is experiencing performance bottlenecks during the training of large models. Profiling has indicated that high-latency I/O operations in the Feature Store are a major contributor, as feature vectors are repeatedly fetched from disk. To mitigate this, an in-memory caching layer for the Feature Store is required. This task involves implementing a configurable Least Recently Used (LRU) cache to reduce disk I/O and accelerate the data retrieval process for model training and inference.

project_spec.name: LexiLearn MVC Orchestrator
project_spec.description:
LexiLearn MVC Orchestrator is an expert-level C-based machine-learning/NLP platform designed to help universities and large K-12 districts build, deploy, and continuously improve adaptive language-learning applications.  The system ingests multimodal classroom data (voice snippets, essays, quiz answers, learning-management logs) and produces individualized feedback and curricula, all while adhering to strict MLOps practices such as hyper-parameter tuning, automated retraining, model monitoring, and model versioning.  LexiLearn’s Model layer encapsulates a full NLP/ML pipeline—data preprocessing, feature engineering via a shared feature store, experiment tracking, and model evaluation—exposed through a Strategy Pattern so that educators can switch among transformer-based summarizers, classical n-gram analyzers, or hybrid models without touching Controller code.

The Controller layer implements a Pipeline Pattern that orchestrates data ingestion from LMS APIs, triggers factory-generated training jobs, logs experiments to the Model Registry, and schedules automated retraining when model drift is detected by Observer Pattern hooks.  The View layer delivers interactive visualizations in the form of real-time dashboards for teachers and curriculum designers, rendering learning-progress heat-maps, feature importances, and model-explainability plots.  MVC separation allows education stakeholders to iterate rapidly on student-facing UX (View) while researchers refine algorithms (Model) and DevOps teams harden deployment workflows (Controller), ensuring that pedagogical goals remain at the core of the development cycle.
dependencies: SentencePiece C library (tokenization for multilingual education content)
LibSVM / LIBLINEAR (classic baselines & quick model benchmarking)
ZeroMQ (event bus implementing Observer Pattern for drift notifications)
cJSON (fast JSON serialization for RESTful model serving)
